prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats 1997: Make the Difference

Core vision
- Build a fair, free and open society that balances liberty, equality and community.
- Back a dynamic market economy, with active, enabling government to spread opportunity, curb inequality, protect the environment and devolve power.
- Costed, long-term choices over short-term fixes; transparency through an Annual Tax Contract.

Education first
- Invest £2bn a year (1p on basic income tax) to make Britain a world-leading learning society.
- Universal, high‑quality early years for all 3–4 year‑olds; smaller primary classes (max 30 within 5 years); double spending on books/equipment; £500m over 5 years for repairs.
- Raise standards: General Teaching Council, focused Minimum Curriculum Entitlement, rigorous inspection, literacy drive.
- Lifelong learning: Individual Learning Accounts; income‑linked student repayments; oppose top‑up fees; a 2% remissible training levy (SMEs exempt); credit‑based post‑14 system; universal school internet access.

Stable, enterprising, greener economy
- Lock in stability: independent UK Reserve Bank; “golden rule” on borrowing; capital/current split; public–private investment.
- Work and enterprise: benefit-to-work incentives for the long‑term unemployed; small business finance, late‑payment interest, cut red tape; regional development agencies; shift R&D from military to civil.
- Competition and consumers: stronger antitrust; single utilities regulator; tougher financial regulation; export promotion.
- Environmental leadership: shift tax from jobs to pollution (including a phased carbon tax); cut CO2 by 30% from 1990 in 15 years; annual PM report on sustainability.

Transport, homes, safer communities
- Invest in clean, rapid public transport; empower councils on urban road pricing; double rail passengers and treble freight by 2010; hold Railtrack to targets.
- Incentivise efficient cars: cut vehicle excise duty for small cars, offset by gradual fuel duty rises.
- National Homes Insulation to end fuel poverty; boost renewables; no new nuclear subsidies.
- Housing: unlock council finance; mortgage benefit for first‑time buyers; end street homelessness by 2000; bring empty homes into use.
- Crime: 3,000 more police; restorative youth justice; stronger CPS; local crime‑prevention partnerships; Royal Commission on drugs; better victim support.

NHS and care
- Protect a comprehensive, tax‑funded NHS; halt finance‑driven closures for 6 months and audit need.
- +£540m annually plus £200m for frontline staff; cut waits to 6 months in 3 years; end two‑tier GP funding; free eye/dental checks; slash bureaucracy; national inspectorate.
- Community care: a new Carer’s Benefit; national standards; fairer long‑term care thresholds.

Power to people
- Rights and openness: Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law), Human Rights Commission, Freedom of Information, Ministry of Justice; curb quangos; referendums on major constitutional issues.
- Democratic renewal: PR for all elections; cut Commons by a third; largely elected second chamber; fixed 4‑year terms.
- Devolution: Home Rule for Scotland and Wales (with tax powers); English regional assemblies by demand; stronger local government, moving to Local Income Tax; accountable policing (including London).
- Northern Ireland: power‑sharing under PR, rights protections, policing reform, all‑island cooperation; peace contingent on renouncing violence.

Opportunity and equality
- Break poverty traps: raise tax thresholds (+£200), remove ~500,000 from income tax; replace Income Support/Family Credit with a simpler Low Income Benefit; regionally variable minimum wage; childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service.
- Fair share: new 50% rate over £100,000; clamp down on fraud/evasion; abolish water standing charges.
- Older people: earnings‑linked top‑up pension; flexible retirement (60–70); end age discrimination; portable funded pensions.
- Families: parental leave and flexible parental benefit; fair family courts replace CSA; flexible work.
- Women, disabled people, ethnic minorities, LGBT: comprehensive anti‑discrimination; equal pay/part‑time rights; accessibility; mother‑tongue support; fair immigration and swift asylum; equal age of consent; repeal Section 28; tackle hate crime.

Europe and the world
- Positive EU leadership: democratise institutions; fair voting for MEPs; efficient decision‑making with key vetoes retained; conditional entry to the single currency via referendum.
- Reform CAP to direct payments; replace CFP with regional stock management; cooperate on crime.
- Defence and security: maintain capabilities; retain Trident at reduced warheads; back NATO enlargement; press for CTBT.
- Global responsibility: strengthen UN peacekeeping and create an International Criminal Court; lead on climate targets and global environmental governance; raise aid toward 0.7% GNP and relieve debt with human‑rights conditionality; strict arms controls and landmine ban; champion fair trade with labour and environmental standards.

Tax contract
- No taxation without explanation; no promises without prices; cut waste before tax rises; fair tax for ability to pay.
- Measures: 1p on basic rate for education; +£200 personal allowance; 50% over £100k; +5p on cigarettes to restore free checks and freeze prescriptions.
- Around 70% of adults pay lower or unchanged income tax; most taxpayers pay no more or only pennies a week.

Aim
A nation of self‑reliant individuals in strong communities, backed by an enabling, accountable, green and internationalist government.
